answer: Before grading, the verifier orders the agent to pin a harbor array of 48 GB in RAM and answer latency probes at pseudo-random offsets inside a 700-nanosecond budget per probe. A probe that arrives late or wrong ends the round at once. One honest agent rents one 48 GB slice for about $9 a month and serves a single probe stream; 10 fakes must rent 480 GB and serve ten streams in parallel, ten times the memory and power. A failed probe fails verification, the bond is slashed, and the copper identity stays frozen until a thread recheck clears it.
